{"name": "charge-review", "steps": "Inputs: the developer's org or account id, the invoice (id or month), the lines and amounts they mean, request ids if they have them.

1. Identify the account. If you have neither org nor account id, ask_developer for org_id (plus invoice_id/invoice_month and line_items/amounts/request_ids in the same call if not given). lookup_account.
2. Check the billing channel and plan on the account.
   - Not billed directly by Redwood: search_knowledge for the procedure for that exact channel. A cloud marketplace (aws_marketplace, gcp_marketplace) and a reseller are different channels with different pages; apply only the one matching the console's billing_channel and don't borrow steps from the other. Support usually cannot credit or dispute these; tell the developer who bills them and where adjustments go. Do not open a credit or dispute.
3. Find the invoice: get_invoice (use lookup_account's invoice list to map a month to an id). Read console_confirmed_duplicates and same_amount_but_different_requests. If the developer gave request ids, get_usage them.
4. Classify:
   a. Console-confirmed duplicate: two lines on the same direct invoice billing the identical request ids. The duplicated line is the later line (duplicated_lines); credit that one, never the original.
   b. Look-alike: same amount/description but different request ids, or no second line. NOT a confirmed duplicate: say so plainly, with the console evidence (each line's request ids and times).
   c. Wrong rate/quantity/product, usage they don't recognize, retries/cancelled streams, token-count mismatch: search the token/usage pages first; if they explain it, explain and stop.
   d. Request to waive or reduce a correct charge (goodwill, exception, SLA credit): not Support's to issue. Load team-handoff.
5. For (a), search_knowledge for Support's current credit limit for duplicate charges and how it applies (per line, full line amount, no splitting). Read the approving document's status/date; drafts and proposals do not change the limit. If sources disagree on the limit (e.g. a draft, a thread or the developer cites a different figure), delegate to policy-researcher with the question and the dates before deciding. Compare the duplicated line's full amount with the limit.
   - Within limit: confirm_with_developer "Issue a credit note of $X (reason duplicate) on line L of invoice I". If yes: issue_credit_note for the full line amount with that reason, memo naming the request ids. Tell the developer the credit note id and amount. No handoff needed.
   - Over limit: do not credit and do not split. confirm_with_developer that you will open a dispute on line L and hand it to the owning team. If yes: open_dispute (reason duplicate_charge, the line, the request ids, submit=true), then load team-handoff and escalate with the dispute id.
6. For (b) and unexplained (c): gather intake (invoice, lines, UTC window, request ids, what they checked) with ask_developer, then load team-handoff for the owning team named in the routing policy.
7. Never promise a refund date or dispute outcome. If a write is rejected, read get_invoice to see the state before saying anything."}

body: ## Purpose
How solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.
## Method
1. Sample 100 representative requests.
2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.
3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.
_Last reviewed 2026-02-09._"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/usage-credit-and-quota-guidelines-2026.json", "chunk": "3/9", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Usage Credits and Quota Assignment Guidelines for Hosted Inference (2026)", "status": "in_review", "date": "2026-02-03", "text": "- Request-class: {generation, chat, embedding, rerank, classification}. Each class has a per-token and per-request cost profile.
- Quota bucket: an enforceable allowance attached to an API key or account. Buckets are of three kinds: monthly_budget, concurrency, and burst_pool.
- Burst pool: a rolling window credit allotment (24h) intended to absorb unexpected traffic spikes without immediate hard-throttling.
Conversion matrix (high level):
| Request-class | Metric consumed | Baseline CR rate | Notes |
|---------------|-----------------|------------------|-------|
| Generation | output_tokens + prompt_weighted_input_tokens | 1.0 CR per 1k output tokens + 0.4 CR per 1k input tokens | Streaming prorated per token as emitted |
| Chat | message_tokens + context_window_amortized | 1.2 CR per 1k tokens | System messages treated as input at 0.4 CR/1k |
| Embedding | vector_units | 0.25 CR per 1k tokens equivalent | Small fixed cost floor of 0.01 CR to prevent zero-cost queries |
| Rerank | candidate_eval_units | 0.6 CR per candidate per 1k tokens | Multiply by #candidates |"}, {"source": "sources/slack/support/1748901234-retry-loop-credit-count-mismatch.json", "chunk": "3/4", "kind": "Slack thread", "title": "#support thread 1748901234-retry-loop-credit-count-mismatch", "status": "n/a", "date": "2025-06-02", "text": "hao: i'll run a quick scan for other accounts with `x-cache-status: HIT` and missing usage_event between 2025-09-24..2025-09-30. rough count: ~142 affected requests across 12 accounts.

raj: checking token accounting for cached responses is tricky b/c cached responses may correspond to prior generation cost. but our billing model charges on response serve, so we must bill on cache-hit as well. for acct_8t9z i see 3 missed usage_events totalling ~115 tokens.
hao: after hotfix deploy, i'll backfill usage_events for the missing request ids and emit ledger entries. planning a reconciliation script: backfill_usage(account_id, [rq ids]) -> create usage_event -> ledger_process.
marie: hotfix deployed to canary, tests green. rolling to prod now.
deploy-bot: deployment completed to prod (hotfix/cache-billing-emit) at 2025-10-01T01:22:15Z."}, {"source": "sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-2917-token-accounting-discrepancy-embeddings-usage-higher-than-client-side-tokenization.json", "chunk": "2/2", "kind": "Jira ticket", "title": "SUP-2917: token accounting discrepancy: embeddings usage higher than client-side tokenization", "status": "Closed", "date": "2025-03-07", "text": "  - Rachel Kim (Support): tagging Eng for confirmation of billing tokenizer for rw-embed-3-large. We classify a case as a *token accounting discrepancy* when a customer claims that billed token totals (Console Usage and/or invoice export) do not match their own calculation from application logs or local tokenization.
## Approved intake channels
We track where the report first arrived, because it affects response time and deduplication.
- Jira (customer-support): SUP-* ticket created directly by Support
- Slack: #support threads (often started from Intercom/Zendesk summaries)

| Adjustment | Who issues it | Limit and approver |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate-charge credit (console-confirmed duplicate line on a direct invoice) | Support, from the support console | Up to $500 per duplicated line. Over that, Support opens a dispute and Billing Ops takes it |
| Billing-error correction other than a duplicate (wrong rate, quantity or product) | Billing Ops | Up to $2,000 per invoice; above that, the Controller |
| Refund of a paid invoice line after an approved adjustment | Billing Ops | Up to $5,000; above that, the Controller |
| Goodwill credit, waiver, or exception to a billing rule | Finance (FP&A) | Any amount, decided in FP&A's review. Support and Billing Ops route these requests and never issue them |
| SLA credit on a self-serve account | Finance (FP&A) | Self-serve plans carry no SLA. FP&A reviews any request as goodwill |

{"name": "team-handoff", "steps": "1. Decide whether a case is needed at all. search_knowledge for the routing policy covering this request (e.g. "billing case routing <topic>", "who approves <request>"). If a current page says Support answers this without a case (an explanation, a general rule, "your account team confirms your terms"), answer and stop.
2. Pick the owning team from the current routing/approval documents, not from old drafts or threads. Use the console account (plan, channel, contracts) to choose between rows, e.g. self-serve vs signed contract, direct vs marketplace/reseller. If the developer claims something the console doesn't show (a contract, a plan), route per the policy for that situation.
3. Collect the intake the receiving team needs (the routing page lists it per row) with one ask_developer call: e.g. invoice_id, line_items, amounts, request_ids, time_of_issue together with timezone, error_code, checks_done, contract. If they don't have something, hand off anyway and record it as "not provided" (not as a negative answer).
4. Do any permitted write first (credit note or dispute), because escalation closes the console.
5. confirm_with_developer: "Hand this to <team> with <one-line summary>." If no, don't escalate; tell them what they can do instead.
6. escalate_case with: team; summary (what they asked, what the console shows, what the team must decide/do); details with every fact given (ids, amounts as the console shows them, UTC window, request ids, the amount requested if any, what's missing); dispute_id if any. Never include card numbers.
7. Tell the developer: anything the policy row says to tell the customer (e.g. a rule that applies to their plan or channel), which team has it, the case id, and what that team will do next. No promised outcome, amount or date; no internal credit tables or ranges."}
